properties.name: Felsőkakas
properties.approximationNote: Felsőkakas: rough rural tract west of the railway and south of Kossuth Lajos utca, joined along visible access-track/field edges. Agricultural rear edge is inferred; the highway is not assumed to be an official neighbourhood limit.

properties.name: Kórházi-dűlő
properties.approximationNote: Kórházi-dűlő: southern town-edge field tract using the Malom-árok bend and the visible agricultural access-track/field pattern. Connections between tracks are inferred; not a cadastral boundary.

properties.name: Kékidűlő
properties.approximationNote: Kékidűlő: the named hillside garden/vineyard tract around Bodzavirág and Barátlakás sor; visible vineyard and access-lane edges guide a coarse connected extent. Not the whole Balaton-felvidék mountain-range polygon.

properties.name: Lakótelep
properties.approximationNote: Lakótelep: housing blocks between the Kéki-patak side and the railway, around Noszlopy/Gyár/Köztársaság/Zrínyi streets. Outer rear plot edges are inferred from the street fabric.

properties.name: Reformkori Városrész
properties.approximationNote: Reformkori Városrész: historic resort street/park fabric around Blaha Lujza, Jókai, Gyógy tér and Tagore sétány, with the northern main-road arc and eastern watercourse/park approach as coarse limits. Municipal tourism pages independently identify this historic quarter; the whole quarter is broader than Gyógy tér park alone.

properties.name: Tamáshegy
properties.approximationNote: Tamáshegy: coarse hill-and-hillside extent above Tamáshegyi/Kilátó streets, following the actual path/woodland edge and hillside street pattern. Northern summit-side closure is inferred, rather than copying the enormous mountain-range footprint.

properties.name: Besenyő
properties.approximationNote: Besenyő: western agricultural tract beside the north-south farm track and motorway curve. The native track junctions and field blocks delimit a rough tract; closure between those features is inferred. The university place-name inventory independently records Besenyő/Besenyői-dűlő.

properties.name: Feketés
properties.approximationNote: Feketés: field block east of the motorway, around the mapped Feketés locality. North/east/south farm tracks guide the extent; short inter-track connections are estimated. It is a rural toponym, not a housing-estate boundary.

properties.name: Gyugy-hát
properties.approximationNote: Gyugy-hát: coarse agricultural ridge tract enclosed by the visible field-access lanes south of the motorway; includes the named ridge rather than a point buffer. Western links and the southern tract reach are approximate. The historical university inventory confirms Gyugy/Gyugypuszta in this locality.

properties.name: Kígyós
properties.approximationNote: Kígyós: agricultural tract southeast of the motorway junction, between the diagonal approach road and mapped field/access edges. It includes both sides of the named field-edge position; exact historical field limits are not known.

properties.name: Tüskés
properties.approximationNote: Tüskés: narrow Séd-side agricultural tract north of the viaduct/motorway, including the mapped ponds/green plots and nearby fields around the name. Water, access lane and highway guide the rough envelope; it is not merely the pond polygon.

properties.name: Diászó
properties.approximationNote: Diászó: the named road-side garden/orchard strip between mapped farm access lanes and the north-south route, extending through the actual plot pattern. This is a broad locality estimate, not the tiny scrub parcel that happens to cover its label.

properties.name: Rigópuszta
properties.approximationNote: Rigópuszta: complete native farmyard footprint covering the name point, supported by two addr:place=Rigópuszta address points. Geometry is source-native; associating the complete farmstead footprint with the locality is a low-confidence extent interpretation, not an official quarter boundary.

properties.name: Csebere
properties.approximationNote: Csebere: northern hillside residential street fabric around Állomás/Krúdy/Móricz/Arany/Ady streets, above the separate Tobruk label and west of the railway. Streets and woodland edge guide a coarse connected boundary; residential rear-edge joins are inferred.

properties.name: Balatonszéplak
properties.approximationNote: Balatonszéplak: coarse western Balaton-shore residential locality around the named point, using the mapped canal, rail corridor and shore-side street grid. The northern shore approach and boundary towards Ezüstpart are inferred from the landward street pattern; not a precise shoreline or tourism-district boundary.

properties.name: Csemetekert
properties.approximationNote: Csemetekert: the complete native orchard/nursery footprint adjoining the locality label and the mapped access-lane junction. Its interpretation as this compact nursery locality is inferred. No wider named neighbourhood boundary was found; this is specifically the site-scale extent, not a claim over surrounding forest.

properties.name: Felsődobos
properties.approximationNote: Felsődobos: road-and-watercourse-guided northern Dobos settlement tract around the Fő utca crossing and the Felsődobos label, separated from Alsódobos to the south. Field-side joins are coarse interpretations; the output does not copy the already mapped Alsódobos footprint.

properties.name: Csillag lakótelep
properties.approximationNote: Csillag lakótelep: older compact estate around Bem József utca, north of the Mártírok útja/Lehár approach; manually encloses the actual housing-site pattern. It is separated from the independently named newer estate to the northeast; rear edges are approximate.

properties.name: Szőny
properties.approximationNote: Szőny: coarse connected historical settlement street-grid extent south of the railway, including the Hősök/Kis/Mikszáth/Ady/Bartók neighbourhood and stream-side rear edge. It is not the whole historical administrative territory; northern industrial/waterfront land and the separate Molaj estate are excluded from this built-locality estimate.

properties.name: Új Csillag lakótelep
properties.approximationNote: Új Csillag lakótelep: newer housing-site and access-loop extent southeast of the pond, north of Táncsics Mihály and northeast of the old Csillag estate. Its connecting plot edges are inferred from the mapped loop and building-site context.

properties.name: Ady lakótelep
properties.approximationNote: Ady lakótelep: compact eastern hillside estate east of the Tési/Kálvária road, following its mapped residential loops and estate-to-hill edge. The municipal planning strategy corroborates the Kálvária-domb–Ady lakótelep urban unit; this is a narrower estate interpretation.

properties.name: Alsóinkám
properties.approximationNote: Alsóinkám: lower town-centre residential fabric around Szent István/Jókai/Fekete Gyémánt/Korompay streets, bounded approximately by the principal street approaches, stream and industrial-side rear blocks. Internal-quarter placement is source-map based; no official perimeter is asserted.

properties.name: Felsőinkám
properties.approximationNote: Felsőinkám: upper residential fabric below the Kálvária slope and west of Tési/Inotai streets, around Munkácsy Mihály and Árpád approaches. The named hillside/road pattern guides a coarse perimeter, with inferred plot-back connections.

properties.name: Kismező
properties.approximationNote: Kismező: northern residential street grid around Krúdy/Viola/Vörösmarty/Herman Ottó/Erkel streets, between the mapped western/eastern stream approaches. The municipal strategy names the Kismező/Erkel/Keszi/Bán streets as a subarea; this broader coarse quarter estimate uses the surrounding street-and-stream fabric rather than copying that subarea as an exact identity.

properties.name: Kálvária
properties.approximationNote: Kálvária: hillside housing blocks around Hegyhát, Róbert Károly, Puskin and Czóbel approaches, east of the Kismező stream and above Felsőinkám. The municipal district street listing corroborates these streets; rear edges are an explicitly rough interpretation.

properties.name: Zobákakna
properties.approximationNote: Zobákakna: former mine/locality grounds around the mapped mine-site footprint and its approach road above the Hóvirág/Gesztenyés streets. The outline includes the landward site and approach plots, not merely a building; short field-side links remain inferred.

properties.name: Tekerespuszta
properties.approximationNote: Tekerespuszta: compact settlement/farmstead around the visible internal lane loop and the Cinca-Csikgát branch. Three source addr:place points corroborate the locality; the complete street-side plot cluster is enclosed with coarse rear edges.

properties.name: Tófarok
properties.approximationNote: Tófarok: rough northern stream-side meadow/garden locality between the Boglárka neighbourhood and Remeteség, following actual trails and the Által-ér/Fácán-patak watercourse pattern. Unmapped transitions between paths are estimated; this is a land-area extent rather than the water surface.

properties.name: Laguna Lakópark
properties.approximationNote: Laguna Lakópark: compact estate around Cserkész/Berettyó/Lemnic/Ruttkai street approaches, west of Nagyszombati út. This narrow street-block interpretation intentionally does not copy the broad Külsőhegy or Öreghegy parent polygons; exact estate plot ownership was not verified.

properties.name: Velinszky László-lakótelep
properties.approximationNote: Velinszky László-lakótelep: complete local estate street/block pattern around Jávor Ottó tér and Ősz utca, south of Szekfű Gyula utca and east of the Várkörút approach. The park alone is not used as the estate polygon; street-side and rear block links are approximate.

properties.name: Ősz utca
properties.approximationNote: Ősz utca: narrow street-neighbourhood extent around the actual Ősz street and adjacent Jávor Ottó tér housing plots. It overlaps the Velinszky estate because the source names may represent different geographic granularities; no unsupported alias/identity is asserted. Approximate block outline, not a road-centreline buffer.

properties.name: Pincesor
properties.approximationNote: Pincesor: contiguous cellar-row roadside locality along the southern village-lane bend. The whole visible cellar plot row and its approach are enclosed, broader than the tiny covering residential polygon; rear parcel connections remain coarse.

properties.name: Juhépuszta
properties.approximationNote: Juhépuszta: small historical farmstead locality at the terminal access-lane loop north of the Hidás-patak crossing. The actual access spur and the nearby watercourse/field pattern guide the irregular site envelope. No official farmstead perimeter or current building completeness is claimed.

properties.name: Bodakajtor
properties.approximationNote: Bodakajtor: connected village/farmstead street fabric around Major/Akácfa streets and the main-road fork, with visible plot-access edges as a coarse outer perimeter. Agricultural rear links are inferred rather than treated as cadastral limits.

properties.name: Suhogó
properties.approximationNote: Suhogó: coarse hillside-to-main-road locality around the Suhogó lane and southern Búza/Boglártelep approaches. The visible access tracks, woodland front and residential plots guide an irregular connected extent; the large Velencei-hegység parent is not copied.

properties.name: Lujzamajor
properties.approximationNote: Lujzamajor: compact farmstead street/access-lane cluster west of the reservoir and Rovákja-patak. Actual intersecting lanes and site plots guide the envelope, with explicitly estimated rear connections; it does not include the reservoir water surface.

properties.name: Rovákja
properties.approximationNote: Rovákja: stream-and-rail-side locality around the named access/trail junction, corroborated by an addr:place point. A connected landward tract is estimated from the actual access network and stream; no whole-mountain polygon or point-radius buffer is used.

properties.name: Bányavölgy
properties.approximationNote: Bányavölgy: complete mapped farmyard/site footprint at the named locality west of Szent László-patak. Source geometry is native; equating that whole farmstead site with the named locality is a low-confidence extent association, not an official neighbourhood polygon.

properties.name: Tokod-Ebszőnybánya
properties.approximationNote: Tokod-Ebszőnybánya: linear settlement strip along the actual mine/hamlet approach road north of the Dági-patak, from the old mine approach towards Tárhya utca. Plot-back connections are rough; the output covers landward settlement context rather than a river or street-centreline buffer.

properties.name: Honvéd lakótelep
properties.approximationNote: Honvéd lakótelep: compact residential quarter around Kertész, Árok and Határ approaches, northeast of the Szabolcsi/main-road junction and south of the railway. Irregular block perimeter is inferred from actual street geometry and plot access.

properties.name: Rózsa Lakópark
properties.approximationNote: Rózsa Lakópark: the connected small housing-site pattern south of Kemping utca and west of the watercourse/Tábor approach. Actual estate lanes and the site-side stream guide its coarse outer edge; rear plot ownership is unverified.

properties.name: Barátlakáspuszta
properties.approximationNote: Barátlakáspuszta: complete native farmyard footprint at the named locality and terminal access lane, west of the watercourse. The geometry itself is source-native; its whole-locality interpretation is an explicitly inferred farmstead association.

properties.name: Botpuszta
properties.approximationNote: Botpuszta: broad connected settlement/farmstead extent around Gesztenyés, Vadvirág, Kápolna, Kossuth and Kolumbusz approaches, including the adjoining farm cluster. Two addr:place points corroborate the locality. Actual road/plot patterns guide an approximate landward perimeter; exact estate or cadastral boundaries are not claimed.

properties.name: Aranyhegyi lakótelep
properties.approximationNote: Aranyhegyi lakótelep: compact hillside estate blocks between the Vörösmarty/Kálvin approaches, distinct in granularity from broad Aranyhegy and nearby Aranyhegyi lakópark names. Actual access lanes and building-plot pattern guide a coarse perimeter; no unsupported identity alias is asserted.

properties.name: Szentgyörgymezői lakópark
properties.approximationNote: Szentgyörgymezői lakópark: northern housing-site street grid around Kopácsy, Szent Kinga, III. Béla and Gizella approaches, above the older Szentgyörgymező label. The estate is treated as a smaller overlapping unit, not aliased to the parent quarter; plot-back links are approximate.

properties.name: Újmajor
properties.approximationNote: Újmajor: complete native farmyard footprint at the major locality east of the Perbáli/Békás stream junction. Its site polygon is source-native; associating that compact whole site with the place name is a low-confidence extent interpretation.

properties.name: Földespuszta
properties.approximationNote: Földespuszta: connected farmstead/estate lane network north of the main-road bend and east of the small stream, including the full visible row of farm/residential plots. Source roads and the site pattern guide the envelope; field-side links are inferred.

properties.name: Viadukt lakópark
properties.approximationNote: Viadukt lakópark: northern street blocks around Szent László/Czipri bíró/Káposztáskert/Búzavirág approaches, west of the stream. This is a compact estate-level interpretation rather than the entire surrounding Katalin-hegy street grid; exact development parcel limits are not verified.

properties.name: Zöldsziget lakópark
properties.approximationNote: Zöldsziget lakópark: connected residential blocks around Rosenbach János, Kinizsi and Angeli András street approaches, west of the main Szily route. The whole street-block site is estimated instead of the tiny covering greenfield parcel; rear plot edges remain low-confidence.

properties.name: Akalacspuszta
properties.approximationNote: Akalacspuszta: coarse rural farm/access-track tract around the named locality west of Paks. The actual irregular field-track circuit provides the envelope; gaps between track segments are inferred. Municipal structural-planning material independently records Akalacs lands. This is not an official rural cadastral boundary.

properties.name: Biritó
properties.approximationNote: Biritó: settlement/farm estate south of the Paks–Kölesd road, including Orgona/Jácint street plots and the associated agricultural site, west of the main bypass. The municipal strategy describes this combined garden-housing and agricultural character. Road/plot rear links are rough rather than surveyed; the separate neighbouring Csámpapuszta label is not silently treated as an alias.

properties.name: Cseresznyéspuszta
properties.approximationNote: Cseresznyéspuszta: rough woodland-edge and farm-track locality extent at this particular source place point, using the adjoining field lanes and southern access junction. Multiple nearby source labels use a similar name, so this is expressly the local named tract, not a verified identity with the entire Cseresznyés external quarter. The municipal structural plan independently records Cseresznyés rural lands.

properties.name: Kishegy
properties.approximationNote: Kishegy: coarse connected urban street fabric around Gesztenyés/Kishegyi and the western/southern housing streets towards Tolnai/6-os road approaches. Municipal ITS describes the broader Kishegy-Újváros unit with Gesztenyés–Kishegyi–Újtemplom–Tolnai–6-os limits; this source-map estimate represents the named Kishegy locality, not every detached part of that planning unit. Plot-edge joins remain approximate.

properties.name: Lakótelep
properties.approximationNote: Lakótelep: panel-estate/site fabric around Barátság/Ifjúság/Babits/Újtemplom approaches, within the broader Kishegy urban unit. Municipal ITS describes the panel-estate band and its adjacent institutional areas. The estimate is narrower than Kishegy and uses actual block/access-road context rather than a parent-quarter copy.

properties.name: Szérűskert
properties.approximationNote: Szérűskert: connected northwestern residential locality around the Pál/Fehérvári side-street pattern and Sárgödör approaches. The municipal CLLD text independently associates Szérűskert with Pál utca, Fehérvári út and side streets. Actual streets and the town-edge site pattern guide the coarse perimeter; the larger Szérűskert-Öreghegy planning unit is not blindly copied.

properties.name: Ipari park
properties.approximationNote: Ipari park: connected industrial-development land beside the main-road/industrial rail access, south of the Ercsi-Gazdasági Vasút site. Includes the mapped industrial-site land and nearby access plots rather than only a small building/water parcel. Exact business-park legal parcel limits are not known; boundaries towards undeveloped land are explicitly inferred.

properties.name: Tiszti lakótelep
properties.approximationNote: Tiszti lakótelep: compact apartment/estate grounds between the inner access lane, Bercsényi/Móricz approaches and the main north-south road. The whole visible housing-site plot pattern is enclosed; rear and shared-ground edges are approximate.

properties.name: Kálváriadomb
properties.approximationNote: Kálváriadomb: eastern hillside residential street fabric around Tölgy, Erdőhát, Mecsek and Kálváriahegy approaches. The actual terraced road/plot pattern guides the irregular envelope, distinct in scale from the neighbouring Kálvária kert and Zsíroshegyalja labels. The outer hillside transition remains a low-confidence interpretation.

properties.name: Nagyszénásalja
properties.approximationNote: Nagyszénásalja: northern garden-residential street fabric below the woodland front around Hóvirág/Ibolya/Nefelejcs/Gyöngyvirág/Kökörcsin approaches. It is a broad hillside locality estimate and may overlap smaller separately named quarters such as Nagyszénáskert; those labels are not asserted to be synonyms. Woodland and street-block joins are coarse, not cadastral.

properties.name: Szuhay-domb
properties.approximationNote: Szuhay-domb: municipal ITS explicitly describes the circuit Ivanich Antal–Dózsa György–Berzsenyi–Szigeterdő–Gyenis Antal streets. The actual modern Ivanich/Dózsa/Berzsenyi linework and Szigeterdő park approach guide this reconstruction south of Dózsa. Municipal street-renaming records establish that former Gyenis was split into Földvár and Vasút sor in 2013; the modern southern approach is used with coarse park-edge connections. No place-point location is invented. Existing OSM-named Szuhajdomb has only a small street-cell estimate NORTH of Dózsa; this source-defined planning extent should be reviewed as a canonicalization/alternative-boundary candidate rather than assumed to be an unrelated second whole quarter. Exact KSH map alignment remains unverified.
